# Sync iCan to Apple Health

> A free, open-source iOS Shortcut that imports glucose readings from the iCan Health / iCan CGM app (Sinocare iCan i3, i6, and Sibionics) into Apple Health on iPhone, with their measurement times (read as UTC+7 on the public converter) and no duplicates. No Android, xDrip+, Juggluco, Nightscout, bridge app or manual entry.

Key facts:

- The iCan app has no built-in Apple Health / HealthKit sync, but its share button exports an `.xls` file.
- This shortcut takes that `.xls` from the share sheet, converts it, and logs each reading with Apple's built-in "Log Health Sample" action.
- Re-syncing never duplicates readings: the shortcut asks Apple Health for its newest reading and imports only newer ones.
- Sync is manual (share → tap), not background.
- Works with exports from the Thai-language iCan app, both the original format and the September 2026 format. Units: mg/dL or mmol/L.
- The shortcut uploads the `.xls` to a converter on Vercel (ican-health-sync.vercel.app/api/convert), which returns the readings and keeps nothing: no database, no accounts. Data does pass through that server; anyone who wants it to stay on a machine they control can self-host (MIT licensed).
- The export has no timezone. The public converter reads times as Thai time (UTC+7), so for wearers in other timezones readings land hours off; they should self-host with their own `CGM_TZ_OFFSET`.

Thai: แอป iCan ซิงค์เข้า Apple Health เองไม่ได้ แต่ใช้คำสั่งลัดฟรีนี้ส่งค่าน้ำตาลเข้าแอปสุขภาพบน iPhone ได้ พร้อมเวลาวัดจริง ไม่ซ้ำ ไม่ต้องกรอกเอง

- [หน้าดาวน์โหลด (ภาษาไทย)](https://ican-health-sync.vercel.app/): install and use, in Thai
- [Download page (English)](https://ican-health-sync.vercel.app/en/): install and use, in English
- [Source code and documentation](https://github.com/Nice0w0/ican-to-apple-health): how it works, troubleshooting, API, self-hosting
